title: The Afternoon Brief: US Open final set; NFL season opens in chaos
dek: Rybakina clinches No. 1 and faces Sabalenka in Saturday's US Open final as the top two seeds contest their first major championship. Across professional sports, opening days produced cascading injuries, criminal investigations, and international expansion.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Friday delivered concrete results across tennis, football, and baseball: the US Open women's field narrowed to its highest-seeded final in 13 years; the NFL season opened with a quarterback collapse, two major injuries that reshaped rosters, and a historic game in Melbourne; and baseball's stretch run tightened with multiple playoff races still undecided.
bottom_line: Friday consolidated power at the US Open while scattering it elsewhere: Rybakina and Sabalenka will contest the first top-two-seed women's final in 13 years Saturday, yet the NFL's opening week delivered a cascade of quarterback and receiver injuries that reshaped defensive plans, de Paula's debut will test whether prospect tools translate at major-league velocity, the Falcons must clarify Tagovailoa's status by Sunday, and the Clippers criminal investigation enters its discovery phase with subpoenas issued and prosecutors pursuing potential federal charges beyond league penalties. The US Open final is Saturday; NFL Week 1 concludes Sunday; the SEC's rescheduled hearing on LSU's status remains pending.
body: The US Open women's final between Elena Rybakina and Aryna Sabalenka represents a rare convergence at the sport's highest level. Rybakina's 3-6, 6-4, 6-4 victory over Coco Gauff on Friday secured her ascent to world No. 1 when rankings update Monday, per the desk's reporting, ending Sabalenka's 99-week reign. Sabalenka advanced by defeating Jessica Pegula 7-5, 6-2. This marks the first US Open final between the top two seeds since 2013, per BBC Sport cited in the reporting. Sabalenka is bidding to become the first woman since Serena Williams in 2014 to win three successive US Open titles; Rybakina, the Australian Open champion, carries momentum into Saturday's match on a surface where she has historically shown less dominance than Sabalenka.

The NFL's opening week exposed fragility across multiple rosters. The Patriots' season-opening loss to Seattle, 13-10 on September 10, began with a 10-0 lead and ended in fourth-quarter collapse: Drake Maye threw three interceptions, including a game-deciding pick with 26 seconds remaining in the end zone at the Seattle 16-yard line. Broadcaster Cris Collinsworth called the final throw indefensible given the Patriots held field-goal range and overtime. That loss was compounded by injury: A.J. Brown, acquired by New England in the offseason to upgrade Maye's receiving options, suffered a high-ankle sprain in the third quarter and is now out at least four weeks. The Seahawks' own season opener came at a cost: QB Sam Darnold exited on the opening drive with a hip injury, and while a fracture was ruled out, further testing remains pending. Drew Lock finished the game.

Friday brought the NFL's international expansion into view: the San Francisco 49ers defeated the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in the first-ever NFL regular season game in Australia, drawing a sell-out crowd of 100,021. The event marks the start of a four-year agreement between the NFL and Melbourne, per Guardian Sport cited in the reporting.

In baseball, the Dodgers removed Shohei Ohtani from the lineup for a minimum of two weeks, placing him on the 15-day injured list to address left knee soreness and right biceps injuries. Ohtani becomes eligible to return September 23, leaving five regular-season games before October. Manager Dave Roberts stated that if it were a postseason game, Ohtani would play, but the team believes the rest will position him better for the playoffs. The Dodgers are calling up prospect Josue De Paula from Double-A Tulsa to debut as early as Friday in Miami, skipping Triple-A entirely. De Paula, the No. 6 prospect on MLB Pipeline's Top 100 and the Dodgers' top-ranked outfield prospect, slashed .303/.401/.547 with 27 homers in 124 Double-A games in 2026, per the reporting. No Dodgers position player has skipped Triple-A under Andrew Friedman's tenure since October 2014.

In non-game news, federal prosecutors in Brooklyn opened a criminal investigation into the Los Angeles Clippers, owner Steve Ballmer, and Kawhi Leonard for alleged salary-cap circumvention via third-party endorsement deals, escalating the matter from NBA penalties to potential federal criminal charges. The SEC removed former NFL players Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris from LSU's roster after the conference filed an amended lawsuit threatening expulsion. LSU president Wade Rousse locked the roster and stated the school would not challenge a Thursday meeting among the other 15 SEC presidents and chancellors; Yahoo Sports reported expulsion was no longer on that meeting's agenda. Former NFL running back LeShon Johnson was sentenced to five years in federal prison for operating a dogfighting ring in Oklahoma, surrendering 190 dogs, the largest number seized from one individual in a federal dogfighting case, per the Department of Justice.

The Falcons face quarterback uncertainty heading into Sunday's Week 1 opener against Pittsburgh: Tua Tagovailoa suffered an oblique injury in Thursday practice and is day-to-day. If Tagovailoa cannot play, Atlanta would turn to Cooper Rush or undrafted rookie Jack Strand. MLB's playoff races tightened as of Friday: the Rays hold a 3-game lead over the Yankees in the AL East; the Phillies lead the first NL Wild Card over the Cubs by 1 game; and the Padres lead the Diamondbacks by half a game for the final NL Wild Card spot.
